response.text:
### 1) What is on the screen
The frame is a black test card, 256 x 240, not a gameplay screen. Top-center white pixel text reads OURANOS, mid-to-bottom row shows four grey blocky ship/tower sprites in increasing size left to right, labeled 1X, 2X, 3X, 4X underneath. The eye goes first to the white OURANOS title in region x95,y12,w66,h16 because it is the highest contrast on a field that is 92.8% one colour, then drops to the largest 4X sprite in region x189,y116,w39,h77. The player is being asked to do nothing I can see - there is no playfield, HUD, prompt, enemy, or objective visible. I cannot see scrolling, animation, collision, sound, or game state.

### 2) Does it look like a real NES game
(a) palette count reads as NES - PASS: measured 3 distinct colours, all in the 64-entry NES palette, well inside the 25 colours on screen ceiling of 12+12+1, with 92.8% backdrop black.
(b) shading is flat, one colour per shape - PASS: sprites use flat grey + white highlight, no gradient banding I can see.
(c) sprites read against background - PASS for 2X-4X, BORDERLINE-FAIL for 1X: grey/white on black $0F backdrop has high contrast, 8 per scanline limit is not stressed, but the 1X sprite is too few pixels to read.
(d) no anti-aliasing and no soft edges - PASS: title, labels, and sprite edges are hard 1px blocks, no blur I can see.
(e) colour changes land on 16 x 16 grid - PASS vacuously: background is solid backdrop with no attribute changes to drift, and sprite blocks sit on roughly 8 x 8 tile steps. Measured size is a multiple of 8 in both directions, so tiles could map.

If impression vs numbers: numbers agree - this is technically NES-legal, but no shipped NES game shipped a bare scale-test as a frame.

### 3) Composition and text
Crowded nowhere, empty almost everywhere. Region x0,y32,w256,h112 is empty black void. All weight sits on bottom strip x28,y108,w212,h118. Focal point is the title in x95,y12,w66,h16, which is not where gameplay would need it because there is no gameplay. Text regions: T1 title OURANOS x95,y12,w66,h16, T2 1X label x32,y210,w16,h10, T3 2X label x70,y208,w16,h10, T4 3X label x120,y208,w16,h10, T5 4X label x192,y208,w16,h10. All are legible at 256 x 240 as block capitals, but worst is T2 1X in x28,y182,w20,h32 including sprite: the sprite above it is ~6x10px, collapses to noise, and the label is smallest and lowest contrast, forcing guessing what the shape is supposed to be.

### 4) What looks AI generated or off
Honest handmade pixels, not AI slop. No pillow shading, no detail without structure, no garbled glyphs, no soft borders I can see. Tells that it is off as a shipped frame, not as AI:
- test-card composition that reads as a prompt: "show 1X-4X scaling" instead of a designed title or level.
- 92.8% dead black with no starfield, HUD, or ground to justify the backdrop.
- 1X sprite below NES readable minimum for an 8x8 or 8x16 object, presented as if it should read.

### 5) Five concrete fixes
1. Region x0,y32,w256,h112: fill dead void with NES starfield on tile grid - keep backdrop $0F black, add 1px $30 white stars snapped to 8px grid and 2x2px $12 blue stars snapped to 16x16 attribute grid, no colour change inside a 16x16 cell.
2. Region x95,y12,w66,h16: move title down by 8 pixels to y20 and add 1px drop-shadow to the south-east in $00 dark grey, keep face in $30 white, to lock it to an 8px tile row and separate from overscan.
3. Region x28,y182,w20,h32: delete unreadable 1X micro-sprite and redraw as minimum 8x16 metasprite using only $10 light grey body + $30 white cockpit, on an 8px grid, keep 1X label below it.
4. Region x24,y210,w200,h16: snap all labels 1X 2X 3X 4X to common baseline y216 and to 8px x-steps, redraw in 8x8 font $30 white on $0F, no half-pixel drift.
5. Region x189,y116,w39,h77: on the 4X hero, replace $30 white cockpit block with $16 red 4x6px rectangle to create a real focal point using a second sprite palette of $0F transparent + $10 grey + $16 red, simplify side dither to flat.

### 6) Scores and machine readable block
NES Authenticity: 8/10 - legal colours and hard tiles, but test-card not a game.
Readability: 6/10 - title and 2X-4X read, 1X does not.
Charm: 3/10 - honest but empty, no world.
